passages.note: Vote page lists Wicks among the Ayes on AB 1228, a sector-specific fast-food wage law; too narrow to establish a general minimum-wage rung.

passages.provision_quote: The hourly minimum wage for fast food restaurant employees shall be twenty dollars ($20) per hour, effective April 1, 2024.
passages.note: Bill text creates a fast-food-only minimum wage set by an appointed Council, annual increases capped at the lesser of 3.5% or CPI-W; the mechanism does not match any single general-minimum-wage rung.

rows.reasoning: AB 1228 (2023-2024), which Wicks voted Aye on, sets a $20/hour minimum wage only for fast-food restaurant employees, raised annually by an appointed Council capped at the lesser of 3.5% or the CPI-W. This shows support for a higher wage floor in that sector but does not establish whether she favors tying the general wage floor to the cost of living automatically ('rises automatically each year without new legislation'), adjusting it only by legislative vote, or any other rung's mechanism for the broader minimum wage the ladder asks about.
needs_source: A record of Wicks's vote or sponsorship on a general (non-sector-specific) California minimum-wage statute, to establish her view on the general wage-floor mechanism this ladder asks about
